mainTopic: Whether חולין בעזרה is a Torah prohibition, and whether a father's power to make his son a נזיר is a special הלכה or חינוך
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא that speaks of a woman's case involving 'two prohibitions.' The גמרא wants to read these as נבילה and חולין בעזרה, which would make bringing חולין into the עזרה a Torah prohibition. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא rejects this: the prohibitions may only look serious and really be מדרבנן. The גמרא then returns to the main question: is a father's power to make his son a נזיר a special הלכה, or is it only חינוך? It suggests this is the מחלוקת between רבי (until two hairs) and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה (until the age of vows). That link is rejected twice, by explaining their argument through the status of a מופלא הסמוך לאיש, first as Torah law against rabbinic law, then as two rabbinic rules. Next the גמרא compares their argument to a ברייתא about the young רבי חנינא, whom רבן גמליאל examined and praised. The boy's words fit רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה well, and the גמרא begins asking how they fit רבי, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא rejects comparing the male to the female
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא closes by refusing to compare a male's case to a female's: the male's case involves one prohibition, while the female's involves two.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. You may say this about a male, since his case involves only one prohibition. Can you say it about a female, whose case involves two prohibitions?
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא. Its speaker rejects an argument that tried to learn the female's case from the male's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone tried to argue that what is allowed for a male should also be allowed for a female. The answer is 'no': the male's case risks only one prohibition, but the female's case risks two. A more serious case cannot be learned from a lighter one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say' (about this case): the opening of a rejection that points out a difference between two cases
A prohibition
Male / female

phrases.english: No, if you say this regarding a male,
since there is only one prohibition,
will you say the same regarding a female,
where there are two prohibitions?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא quoted just before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the female's case from the male's case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The female's case is more serious (two prohibitions against one), so it cannot be derived from the male's.

steps.title: Reading the 'two prohibitions' as Torah prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the 'two prohibitions' are and suggests they are נבילה and חולין בעזרה, which would show that חולין בעזרה is forbidden מן התורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are these two prohibitions? Aren't they the prohibition of נבילה and the prohibition of bringing חולין into the עזרה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that is really building a proof. It says the two prohibitions must be eating נבילה and bringing חולין into the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבילה is clearly a Torah prohibition. If the ברייתא counts חולין בעזרה right next to it as one of the 'two prohibitions,' it seems to treat חולין בעזרה as a Torah prohibition too. That matters for the earlier question of whether the son's offerings would be a real Torah problem.

keyTerms.meaning: What?
'Is it not...?': a question that leads into a proof
An animal that died without proper שחיטה, forbidden to eat
Bringing non-sacred animals into the Temple courtyard

steps.whyThisMatters: If חולין בעזרה is a Torah prohibition, it is hard to say a father makes his son a נזיר just for חינוך. That reading would lead the son to commit a Torah prohibition.

phrases.english: What are the two prohibitions?
Is it not the prohibition of נבילה,
phrases.notes: The female's bird offering is killed by pinching its neck. If it is not truly sacred, eating it would be eating a נבילה.

phrases.english: and the prohibition of non-sacred animals in the Temple courtyard?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the ברייתא's words 'two prohibitions.'
steps.raayaObject: That bringing חולין into the עזרה is a Torah prohibition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא lists it alongside נבילה as one of 'two prohibitions.'

steps.title: רב אחא: maybe they only look like two prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא rejects the proof. Perhaps the ברייתא means the case only looks like two prohibitions, while really they are only מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא objected: Maybe a person is held responsible here because it looks like two prohibitions, even though they are only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא pushes back on the proof from the previous step. He shows that the ברייתא's words can be read another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never said the two prohibitions are Torah-level. They could be rabbinic prohibitions that look like Torah ones, so we avoid them. So the ברייתא does not prove that חולין בעזרה is forbidden מן התורה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He objects to it': a sage challenging the previous statement
'But perhaps': offers another possible reading
It appears / it looks like
By rabbinic law, as opposed to Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the ברייתא falls away. 'Two prohibitions' may only mean something that looks like two prohibitions on a rabbinic level, so it is still open whether חולין בעזרה is a Torah prohibition.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa son of Rav Ika objected to this:
But perhaps one is held liable for it
because it looks like two prohibitions
by rabbinic law!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that חולין בעזרה is a Torah prohibition.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Two prohibitions' could mean rabbinic prohibitions that only look like Torah ones.

steps.title: A ברייתא: how long can a father make his son a נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the earlier question is already a מחלוקת תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא: רבי says the father can do it until the son shows two hairs (puberty), and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says only until the son reaches the age of vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a מחלוקת between תנאים? Until when can a father make his son a נזיר? Until the son develops two hairs, says רבי. רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה says: until he reaches the age of vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main question: is a father's power to make his son a נזיר a special הלכה, or is it חינוך? It sets up the next move by quoting a ברייתא that might be the same argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two time limits are given. רבי's limit is later: two hairs, the sign of adulthood. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's limit is earlier: the age of vows, when a boy understands vows well enough to make his own. The next step will explain why this difference might match the הלכה-versus-חינוך debate.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall we say it is like a מחלוקת of תנאים?': suggests an older מחלוקת matches the current one
Imposes a vow on someone else
Two hairs: the physical sign of adulthood
The age of vows: the stage just before adulthood when a child's vow can take effect if he understands it

steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' (רבי) here is a specific person: רבי יהודה הנשיא. It is not a general title.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is a dispute between תנאים?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the question from earlier on the דף: is the father's vow a special הלכה, or is it חינוך?

phrases.aramaic: עַד מָתַי מַדִּיר אֶת בְּנוֹ בְּנָזִיר —
phrases.english: Until when may a father vow that his son be a nazirite?
Until the son develops two hairs;
these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
Until he reaches the age of vows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side question about חולין בעזרה and returns to the main question of הלכה versus חינוך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: a father may make his son a נזיר until two hairs. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: only until the age of vows.

steps.title: Matching the ברייתא to הלכה versus חינוך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי holds it is a special הלכה, so the father keeps his power until puberty. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds it is for חינוך, so the power ends once the son can make his own vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a מחלוקת of תנאים? רבי holds it is a special הלכה for נזיר, so even after the son reaches the age of vows, the father keeps vowing for him until he develops two hairs. רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה, who says until the age of vows, holds it is to train him in מצוות. Once the son is out of the father's control, the father is no longer obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each תנא gave his time limit. It ties their two limits to the two sides of the earlier question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father's power is a special הלכה from Sinai, it is not tied to training, so it can last until the son is a full adult (רבי). If it is only חינוך, the father's job ends once the son is mature enough to make his own vows (רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה). The question 'מאי לאו' shows this is still only a suggestion that the גמרא may test.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it not that...?': offers an explanation as a suggestion
It is a special received הלכה about נזיר (a הלכה למשה מסיני)
To train him in מצוות (חינוך)
He has left his (father's) control

steps.whatToRemember: Proposed parallel: רבי (until two hairs) matches the 'special הלכה' view. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה (until the age of vows) matches the 'חינוך' view.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this matching holds, the later debate about the father's power simply repeats an older מחלוקת between תנאים.

phrases.english: Is it not a dispute between תנאים?
For Rabbi holds it is a special הלכה regarding a nazirite,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּהִגִּיעַ לְעוֹנַת נְדָרִים,
phrases.english: and so even though the son has reached the age of vows,
the father keeps on vowing for him
until he develops two hairs.
And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
until he reaches the age of vows,
holds it is in order to train him in מצוות,
and since the son has left his father's control,
the father is no longer obligated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא quoted in step 4 and ties it to the הלכה-versus-חינוך question.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה-versus-חינוך question is a מחלוקת between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The different time limits of רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה in the ברייתא.

steps.title: No, both sides agree it is a special הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from Step 5. Both תנאים may agree that a father making his son a נזיר is a special הלכה. Their real argument is about a מופלא הסמוך לאיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: No. Everyone agrees it is a special הלכה about a נזיר. Here they argue about a child who is close to becoming an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the proof in Step 5 does not work. Both רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה may hold it is a הלכה, and their argument is about something else. The next step explains that other argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 tied the two ages (puberty vs. age of vows) to הלכה vs. חינוך. Now the גמרא moves the argument to a different question: the status of a child in the year before adulthood, whose vows already count. So the מחלוקת תנאים does not have to match the earlier question.

keyTerms.meaning: They say (introduces a reply, often a rejection)
Everyone agrees
A child in the year just before adulthood, whose vows count if he understands them
They argue about

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ages. 'Two hairs' is full adulthood (puberty). The age of vows (עונת נדרים) is the year before that, when the child is a מופלא הסמוך לאיש.

phrases.english: They say: No.
phrases.notes: This means the proof from Step 5 is not a must.

phrases.english: Everyone agrees it is a special הלכה regarding a נזיר,
and here they argue about a child close to adulthood.
phrases.notes: This is the child in the year before adulthood, whose own vows already count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the link made in Step 5 between the מחלוקת תנאים and הלכה vs. חינוך.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה must argue about הלכה vs. חינוך.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument can be explained a different way: both hold it is a הלכה, and they argue about the status of a מופלא הסמוך לאיש.

steps.title: Torah law versus rabbinic law for a child close to adulthood
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that the status of a מופלא הסמוך לאיש is only מדרבנן, so the Torah-level הלכה of the father pushes it aside. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds the status is מדאורייתא, so the father's power ends at the age of vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי holds: a child close to adulthood is only a rabbinic status, so the Torah-level rule comes and pushes aside the rabbinic one. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds: a child close to adulthood is a Torah-level status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains each side of the first rejection. It shows how each age in the ברייתא fits if both agree the father's power is a הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the father's הלכה is Torah law and beats the rabbinic status of the near-adult child, so the father keeps his power until puberty. For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the near-adult child's status is also Torah law, so the father's power stops at the age of vows. The father's power is a הלכה in both views.

keyTerms.meaning: Rabbinic law
Torah law
Pushes aside, overrides

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי סָבַר: מוּפְלָא הַסָּמוּךְ לְאִישׁ — דְּרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: רבי holds: a child close to adulthood is a rabbinic status,
so the Torah-level rule comes and pushes aside the rabbinic one.
phrases.notes: The Torah-level rule is the father's special הלכה to make his son a נזיר.

phrases.english: And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds:
a child close to adulthood is a Torah-level status.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי סָבַר: מוּפְלָא הַסָּמוּךְ לְאִישׁ — דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how each תנא's view fits the first rejection in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Completes the first rejection by giving each side a reason that does not depend on הלכה vs. חינוך.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The different ages come from whether a מופלא הסמוך לאיש is Torah law or rabbinic law, not from whether the father's power is a הלכה.

steps.title: Or both agree it is for חינוך, and argue whether one rabbinic rule overrides another
steps.stepSummary: A second rejection: both may agree the father's power is for חינוך and that the status of a מופלא הסמוך לאיש is מדרבנן. רבי holds the rabbinic rule of חינוך pushes aside the rabbinic status of the near-adult child. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds it does not, so the father's power ends at the age of vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: everyone agrees it is to train him in מצוות, and a child close to adulthood is only a rabbinic status. רבי holds: the rabbinic rule of חינוך comes and pushes aside the rabbinic status of a child close to adulthood. And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who said 'until he reaches the age of vows,' holds: the rabbinic rule of חינוך does not come and push aside the status of a child close to adulthood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to reject Step 5. This time both sides agree it is for חינוך, and they argue about whether one rabbinic rule can override another rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rules here are only מדרבנן, so the question is which one wins. רבי says חינוך wins, so the father keeps his power until puberty. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says חינוך does not win, so his power stops when the son's own vows start to count. So the מחלוקת תנאים cannot prove anything about הלכה vs. חינוך.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
Training a child in מצוות
The age of vows, when a child's own vows begin to count

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to make רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה match the question of הלכה vs. חינוך is rejected twice. (1) Both say הלכה, and they argue whether a מופלא הסמוך לאיש is Torah law or rabbinic law. (2) Both say חינוך, and they argue whether rabbinic חינוך overrides the rabbinic status of a מופלא הסמוך לאיש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא. A מחלוקת תנאים cannot be used to settle a later argument if it can be explained in other ways.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
everyone agrees it is in order to train him in מצוות,
and a child close to adulthood is a rabbinic status.
רבי holds: the rabbinic rule of חינוך comes
and pushes aside the rabbinic status of a child close to adulthood.
And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה,
who said 'until he reaches the age of vows,'
phrases.notes: This quotes his words from the ברייתא in Step 4.

phrases.english: holds: the rabbinic rule of חינוך does not come
and push aside the status of a child close to adulthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כְּדֵי לְחַנְּכוֹ בְּמִצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, separate rejection of Step 5, this time assuming both sides hold חינוך.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Again rejects the claim that the מחלוקת תנאים must be about הלכה vs. חינוך.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even if both hold חינוך, the different ages can come from whether one rabbinic rule (חינוך) overrides another (מופלא הסמוך לאיש).

steps.title: Suggesting the argument matches an older story about רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the argument between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is the same as an argument in a ברייתא about רבי חנינא. The first view there says רבן גמליאל checked the boy for two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this argument is just like another argument between תנאים? A ברייתא teaches: רבי חנינא's father made him a נזיר, and he was brought to רבן גמליאל. רבן גמליאל checked him to see whether he had grown two hairs or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether our argument already appears elsewhere, and it begins quoting a ברייתא story to show this. This sets up the comparison that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first view of the story, רבן גמליאל checks for two hairs. That means two hairs is what decides whether the father's vow still works, which matches רבי's view from Step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It opens a suggestion that may later be rejected.
These תנאים are like those תנאים. Two arguments are really the same argument.
An incident or story that happened
That he made a vow on him. Here, the father made the son a נזיר.
Two hairs, the sign of physical adulthood

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי כִּי הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי,
phrases.english: Shall we say these תנאים are like those תנאים,
phrases.notes: 'These תנאים' are רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה from Step 4.

phrases.english: as it is taught: an incident with רבי חנינא
whose father vowed that he should be a נזיר,
and they brought him before רבן גמליאל.
And רבן גמליאל was examining him
to know whether he had grown two hairs,
or whether he had not grown them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי כִּי הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rejections in Steps 6-8, the גמרא tries a new way to tie the argument in Step 4 to an earlier source.
steps.raayaObject: The argument between רבי (until two hairs) and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה (until the age of vows)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about רבן גמליאל examining רבי חנינא

steps.title: רבי יוסי says the check was for the age of vows
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבי יוסי says רבן גמליאל checked whether the boy had reached the age of vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: רבן גמליאל checked to know whether the boy had reached the age of vows or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second view of what רבן גמליאל was checking. This sets up the two sides that the גמרא wants to match with רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the deciding line is the age of vows, not two hairs. This matches רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view from Step 4, so the ברייתא seems to contain the same argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The age of vows, when a child understands vows well enough for his own vows to count
Or not

phrases.english: רבי יוסי says:

phrases.aramaic: לֵידַע אִם הִגִּיעַ לְעוֹנַת נְדָרִים, אִם לָאו.
phrases.english: to know whether he had reached the age of vows or not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second opinion inside the ברייתא quoted in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The check was for the age of vows, not for two hairs.

steps.title: The boy's clever answer and רבן גמליאל's praise
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא tells רבן גמליאל not to bother checking. Either way he will be a נזיר, because of his father if he is a minor, or because of himself if he is an adult. רבן גמליאל kisses him and predicts he will become a great teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: The boy said: 'My teacher, don't trouble yourself to examine me. If I'm a minor, I'll be a נזיר because of my father. If I'm an adult, I'll be a נזיר because of myself.' רבן גמליאל stood up, kissed him on his head, and said: 'I am sure this boy will one day rule on הלכה in ישראל.' They said: not long after, he was already giving rulings in ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the story. The boy settles the doubt by accepting נזירות in a way that works whichever stage he is at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The boy's point is that the checking doesn't matter. If his father's vow still works, he is a נזיר through it. If it no longer works, he accepts נזירות on himself right now. The גמרא will next test which view these exact words fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't trouble yourself
A minor

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּנְשָׁקוֹ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: רבן גמליאל stood up and kissed him on his head,
he said: I am certain about this one
that he will rule on הלכה in ישראל.
They said: only a little time passed

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, אַל תִּצְטַעֵר לְבוֹדְקֵנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא story that began in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The boy accepts נזירות in a way that works whether or not his father's vow still applies.

steps.title: The boy's words fit רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the boy's words fit well with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who says the father's power lasts until the age of vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who said the father's power lasts until the son reaches the age of vows. That is why the boy said, 'If I am a minor, I'll be a נזיר because of my father.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the boy's words fit one side of the argument. This sets up a challenge against the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, 'minor' means below the age of vows, so the father's vow still works. Above that age the boy can vow for himself. So the boy's two options line up neatly with this view.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... It usually comes before 'but for the other view there is a problem.'
That is why he said

phrases.english: It works well according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה,
who said: until he reaches the age of vows,
that is why he said
'If I am a minor, I will be a נזיר because of Father.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the boy's words from Step 11 to test the views from Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion in step 9 that the story of רבי חנינא matches the argument between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The boy's two options fit neatly if the line falls at the age of vows (רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה). This prepares the contrast in step 13, where the same words are hard to fit to רבי.

steps.title: How do the boy's words fit רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to ask how the boy's line 'if I am an adult, I'll be a נזיר because of myself' fits רבי, who says the father's power lasts until two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי, who said the father's power lasts until the boy grows two hairs, what does 'and if I am an adult, I'll be a נזיר because of myself' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the link between רבי and the story. The question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the line between 'minor' and 'adult' is two hairs, not the age of vows. The גמרא finds it hard to fit the boy's second line to that view. The full explanation of the difficulty and its answer come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: But. Here it turns from the view that fits to the view that is difficult.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two names. רבי says two hairs. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the age of vows.

phrases.english: But according to רבי,
who said: until he grows two hairs,
'and if I am an adult, I will be a נזיר because of myself' — what does this mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי, דְּאָמַר: עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'בשלמא... אלא' structure begun in Step 12 by turning to the view that is harder to explain.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי's view matches the story of רבי חנינא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי, 'adult' is set by two hairs, and the boy's second line seems hard to read that way.
